question: Which segment-specific markers separate proximal tubule, distal early, distal late, and duct in the zebrafish pronephros, and what are their verified IDs?
direct_answer: The evidence bundle does NOT contain the segment-specific marker panel needed to answer this question with verified IDs. Based on established zebrafish pronephros literature (Wingert et al., Development), the canonical segmental markers are: proximal tubule (proximal convoluted = slc20a1a; proximal straight = trpm7/slc13a1), distal early = slc12a1, distal late = slc12a3, and pronephric duct = gata3. However, NONE of these gene symbols or their ENSDARG identifiers appear in the provided evidence bundle, so I cannot verify any ID against the authoritative resolver (Ensembl/ZFIN). The retrieved corpus item (CORPUS-2026-0003) concerns Prkc iota/zeta polarity proteins in tubulogenesis, and the external PMIDs concern frataxin (fxn) and Fibronectin/Hand2 (fn/hand2) — none provide a segment marker panel. The only markers explicitly named in the bundle are pax2 and ATPα1a.1 (atp1a1a.1), which are general specification markers, not segment discriminators. I am therefore flagging this as an evidence gap and providing the standard answer only as literature-based context, NOT as verified from this bundle.
